people.job.role: Blameless man from Uz who suffers and questions God
people.job.relations: His wife speaks to him once. Eliphaz, Bildad, Zophar, and Elihu argue with him.
people.job.meaning: He loses his animals, servants, children, and health. He says he is innocent and asks God for a hearing. The Lord answers him from a whirlwind. Job prays for his friends, and the Lord gives him twice as much.
people.job-wife.relations: She is Job’s wife. Later Job says his breath offends her.
people.job-wife.meaning: She sees Job covered with sores. She asks if he still holds to his integrity. She tells him to renounce God and die. Job calls her words foolish and does not sin with his lips.
people.eliphaz-job.relations: He comes with Bildad and Zophar to comfort Job. The Lord speaks to him in chapter 42.
people.eliphaz-job.meaning: He sits silent with Job for seven days. Then he asks who ever perished while innocent. In chapter 22 he says Job wronged the poor and widows. The Lord says he spoke wrongly, and he brings an offering.
people.bildad.role: Shuhite friend who points to earlier generations
people.bildad.meaning: He tells Job to ask earlier generations. He suggests Job’s children died for their sin. He describes the end of the wicked in chapter 18. After a short third speech, he later joins the offering the Lord commands.
people.zophar.role: Naamathite friend who tells Job to put away sin
people.zophar.meaning: He says God punishes Job less than his sin deserves. He tells Job to put away sin. In chapter 20 he says the joy of the wicked is short. Job answers that the wicked often live long and grow strong.
people.elihu-job.role: Young Buzite who speaks after the three friends
people.elihu-job.meaning: He grows angry at Job and at the three friends. He says God teaches people through dreams and pain. He ends by describing God’s power in the storm. No one answers him, and the Lord speaks next.
people.barachel-family-job.meaning: The text names Barachel only as Elihu’s father. It names Ram only as Elihu’s family. Neither one speaks or acts.
people.job-first-children.role: Seven sons and three daughters who die in chapter 1
people.job-first-children.relations: They are Job’s children. A messenger reports that they are dead.
people.job-first-children.meaning: The sons hold feasts in turn and invite their three sisters. Job offers burnt offerings for them afterward. A great wind knocks down the oldest brother’s house while they feast. The messenger says they are dead.
people.job-messengers.role: Four survivors who bring Job bad news
people.job-messengers.meaning: Four messengers reach Job one after another. Each says he alone escaped. Three of them arrive while the one before still speaks. Job then tears his robe, falls to the ground, and worships.
people.sabeans-job.meaning: They attack while the oxen plow and the donkeys feed. They take the animals and kill the servants with the sword. One servant escapes and tells Job. This is the first loss Job hears about.
people.chaldeans-job.meaning: They form three bands and sweep down on the camels. They take the camels and kill the servants. One servant escapes and tells Job. The news about Job’s children comes right after.
people.jemimah.meaning: Job names her after the Lord restores him. The text calls Job’s daughters the most beautiful women in the land. Job gives her an inheritance among her brothers.
people.keziah.meaning: Job names her second of his three later daughters. The text says no women in the land were so beautiful. She receives an inheritance among her brothers.
people.keren-happuch.meaning: Job names her third of his three later daughters. The text praises the daughters’ beauty. Her father gives her an inheritance among her brothers.
people.job-later-sons.meaning: Job has seven sons after the Lord restores him. The text does not name them. Their sisters share the inheritance with them. Job lives to see four generations of his family.
people.job-siblings.role: Family and friends who comfort Job at the end
people.job-siblings.relations: They are Job’s brothers, sisters, and people who knew him before.
people.job-siblings.meaning: They come to Job’s house and eat bread with him. They comfort him for all the evil that came on him. Each one gives him a piece of money and a gold ring.
people.satan-job.role: Accuser who questions why Job fears God
people.satan-job.relations: He speaks with the Lord twice. He does not appear after chapter 2.
people.satan-job.meaning: He comes before the Lord among God’s sons. He says Job fears God only because God protects him. The Lord puts Job’s goods in his power, and disasters follow. Then he strikes Job with painful sores.
people.adam.meaning: Job names Adam once. Job says he did not hide his sin as Adam did. In Genesis 3, Adam hides from God among the trees.
places.jordan.summary: In chapter 40, the Lord describes behemoth. The animal stays calm when the Jordan swells to its mouth.
places.jordan.limits: The marker shows the river’s general location. The poem does not say where behemoth lives.
sources.web.limits: The text keeps each speaker’s claims. The Lord does not approve every speech.
sources.atlas.limits: Use the map labels as background. The linked atlas also includes LDS commentary.
sources.atlas-canaan.limits: The map positions are estimates. A town marker does not prove each Genesis event.
sources.luther-job.limits: This is a teaching overview of the book as writing. It gives no exact date or place for Job’s life.
sources.luther-job-background.limits: This is a possible setting for the writing. It is not evidence that the events happened during the exile.
sources.luther-job-issues.summary: The study looks at comfort that harms, rival explanations, and Job’s repeated cries to God.
sources.luther-job-issues.limits: This review gives Uz no sure location. Readers explain the final speeches in different ways.
sources.seow-job-excerpt.summary: Seow separates the patient Job of the opening from the protesting Job in the speeches.
sources.seow-job-excerpt.limits: The full commentary was not read. The excerpt gives background on the writing, not a verse-by-verse review.
sources.wikipedia-job.limits: This is encyclopedia background only. Disputed dates and readings need review in scholarly sources.
sources.lds-job-111.limits: Some chapters receive only a general summary. The lesson uses religious sources to say Job was a real person. This is Church teaching, not separate historical proof.
sources.lds-job-112.limits: Chapters 20–37 receive a brief general overview. Linked talks and videos were not reviewed. Later teaching is separate from the passage’s wording.
sources.met-327369.limits: It shows that one region marked its weights. It does not prove what standard weight Israel used.
chapters.*.mapNote: Job lives in the land of Uz. No one knows for sure where Uz was.
chapters.40.mapNote: The point shows the Jordan, which the poem names. It does not show Job’s home.
